summary:
Week 5 was like watching "The Empire Strikes Back" - the powerhouses dominated, the underdogs got frozen in carbonite, and somewhere in the galaxy, Langland's lineup decisions made Jar Jar Binks look like a strategic genius. Let's break down this week's action where mjgrana dropped 173.04 points like he was Thor bringing down the hammer on Thanos, while Langland's 40.3 was more like watching the Titanic sink in slow motion - you knew disaster was coming, but you couldn't look away.

Cosmohouck continues his reign of terror at the top of the power rankings, and Jonathan Taylor's 30.1 points was the centerpiece of a 134.36-point beatdown of Seananigans. That's like the Death Star fully operational - you see it coming, you know what it can do, but you're still helpless to stop it. Meanwhile, Trevor Lawrence added 26.2 in support, and this team is humming like the Millennium Falcon after Han finally fixed the hyperdrive. But let's talk about our hero of the week: mjgrana, aka "The Infinity Gauntlet," who snapped his fingers and made tr4sh's playoff hopes disappear with a 47.98-point victory. Kyren Williams (27.1) and Baker Mayfield (26.7) were like the dynamic duo in "Lethal Weapon" - different styles, perfect chemistry, absolute devastation.

Now for our villain of the week, and I'm not talking about a complex, sympathetic villain like Killmonger - I'm talking about the kind of villain who ties people to railroad tracks. Langland, or as I'm now calling him "The Benchwarmer General," managed to leave approximately 126 points on his bench while starting players who combined for the scoring output of a Pop Warner team. This wasn't just bad luck - this was "The Sixth Sense" level plot twist, except instead of realizing you've been dead the whole time, you realize your entire roster was alive and you left them in street clothes. Jalen Tolbert and Dont'e Thornton combining for a cool 0.0 points while better options gathered dust on the bench? That's like having Indiana Jones on your bench and starting a random archaeology grad student to retrieve the Ark of the Covenant.

The week's other storylines read like a Marvel movie marathon. Tishathefish's 65.88-point demolition of Langland was the equivalent of the Hulk smashing Loki repeatedly - brutal, one-sided, and oddly satisfying to watch. Jaxon Smith-Njigba (23.2) and Tua Tagovailoa (22.7) were dealing, while Langland's Spencer Rattler (15.6) was his high scorer, which is like saying the best part of "The Last Airbender" movie was the opening credits. Meanwhile, mastab24 survived drobs in the week's closest matchup at 10.30 points, with Rachaad White's 21.1 proving to be the difference - that's the fantasy football equivalent of Han Solo shooting first. Sometimes you just gotta take the shot.

The moral of Week 5? Jonathan Taylor is box office gold, cosmohouck is directing a Best Picture winner, and Langland just starred in "Gigli 2: The Benchening." Run the tape!
